record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.context_brief: Freeze-out snapshots as evidence for deconfinement
record.original_question: Can combined measurements of absolute strangeness and charm yields, relative hadron yields, collision energy, and participating amount of matter provide enough chemical-freeze-out snapshots to determine whether deconfinement occurred in relativistic nuclear collisions?

evidence.quote: We thus have, in the absolute yields of strangeness and charm, a measure of the initial stage of the collision and in the relative hadron yields a snap-shot picture of the freeze-out conditions. Can this information illuminate the issue of deconfinement? Definitively so, if we are able also to obtain many different snap-shots of the chemical freeze-out, varying energy of colliding nuclei, and the participating amount of matter.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In relativistic nuclear collisions, consider the following observables associated with the hot fireball created in the collision: (i) the absolute yields of strange and charm quarks produced in the initial partonic stage; (ii) the relative yields of the various hadron species emerging at chemical freeze-out (the stage at which inelastic hadronic interactions cease and particle abundances are fixed); (iii) the center-of-mass collision energy per nucleon pair √s_NN; and (iv) the number of nucleons participating in the collision (typically controlled by varying nuclear size and collision centrality). Each set of measurements at a given (√s_NN, participant number) yields a "snapshot" of the chemical freeze-out conditions, characterized by a temperature T and baryochemical potential μ_B obtained by fitting a statistical hadronization model. Deconfinement is said to have occurred if, during the initial stage of the collision, the matter passed through a phase in which colored quark and gluon degrees of freedom were liberated from hadronic confinement (a quark–gluon plasma).

Question: Does the family of chemical-freeze-out snapshots produced by varying √s_NN and the participant number, together with the absolute strangeness and charm yields and the relative hadron yields at each point, provide sufficient information to determine unambiguously whether deconfinement occurred in the initial stage of such collisions?
artifact.status_search_result: Since 1998 a large body of experimental work at SPS, RHIC, and LHC has used precisely this program — varying collision energy and system size while measuring strangeness/charm yields and hadron ratios — to map the chemical freeze-out curve and to argue for deconfinement (e.g., strangeness enhancement, J/ψ suppression and regeneration, statistical-hadronization fits). The community broadly regards deconfinement as established at top RHIC and LHC energies, while the precise onset and the interpretation of various signatures (especially in the RHIC Beam Energy Scan region) remain under active investigation. Thus the original question is partially answered: the methodology has indeed yielded strong evidence for deconfinement, though pinning down the boundary and a critical point is ongoing.

status_evidence.title: The Phases of QCD (BNL/RHIC)
status_evidence.snippet: Measurements at RHIC have provided strong evidence for the formation of a quark-gluon plasma, a deconfined state of matter.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental program using strangeness, hadron yields, and energy/system-size scans has produced evidence for deconfinement.

status_evidence.title: Decoding the phase structure of QCD via particle production at high energy (Andronic et al., Nature 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Statistical hadronization analysis of particle yields across energies traces the chemical freeze-out line and supports a deconfinement transition.
status_evidence.claim: Chemical-freeze-out snapshots across collision energies/systems support the deconfinement scenario.

status_evidence.title: RHIC Beam Energy Scan
status_evidence.snippet: The Beam Energy Scan program varies collision energy to search for the onset of deconfinement and a possible QCD critical point.
status_evidence.claim: The questions of onset of deconfinement and critical point remain actively studied via energy/system-size scans.
